Brain on fire - Encephalitis

By: Dezi Rorich | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A YOUNG SOUTH AFRICAN GIRL ATTACKED BY A MYSTERY BRAIN ILLNESS TURNS FROM ANGEL TO DEMON OVERNIGHT

Summary:
Carte Blanche meets a young South African girl who turned from an “Angel to a Demon”. Angelica’s over-night, radical personality change made those close to her worry that she had been possessed by a demonic force! Instead, she had become the latest victim of mystery illness.

Further information:
An exploration into a relatively newly diagnosed brain disease Anti-NMDA (N-methyl D-aspartate) receptor encephalitis that infects mostly young women. It is an acute form of encephalitis that is potentially lethal but has high probability for recovery if diagnosed early. Symptoms can include paranoia, mania, being dazed, personality changes, acting "possessed" and being catatonic, which can lead some medical professionals to diagnose the problem as psychological instead of physical. The autoimmune disease (first identified in 2007 by Dr Josep Dalmau) occurs when antibodies turn on the brain and cause it to swell.

2. We need to make more of the real moments. The viewer won’t get the reality of the calls if you don’t tell us... you have to label them ‘Actual Cellphone Footage’ on the hospital footage once at the beginning of a clip and again at the end
3. And say in script IN THIS MOMENT etc.
4. The front is quite top heavy and you can reduce it a bit to get to Mochan sooner. Too much of the symptoms before we hear its a disease – bring in sooner that this an auto immune disease
5. The link at the end with the blue light on it feels out of place with the rest of the story – rather write it into script...
6. Be very careful about the choice... must be really subtle don’t milk the drama
7. Structurally I think that its very sound...
8. You must come down to 12 minutes
9. Jean: family friend – and you can call her a close family friend in your script...
10. Zoom in the shot of Derek in the reversal on the Skype interview
11. Makes sure where she says 13 Feb you are referring to last year in your script – clarify that for audience.
12. Hard to understand Najjar. Sub title his whole interview and you can reduce some of what he said.

Press Release:


Brain on fire
Overnight, a mysterious form of encephalitis dramatically and terrifyingly alters a young woman’s personality. Her brain feels as though it is on fire. Doctors are baffled and outsiders would be forgiven for believing she has been possessed by a demonic force. Carte Blanche asks how many more patients committed to psychiatric wards, could in fact have this very same disease – but remain undiagnosed?


Script:


(START Studio Intro) – NOT RECORDED
Tonight Carte Blanche meets a young South African girl who turned from an “Angel to a Demon”. Angelica’s over-night, radical personality change made those close to her worry that a demonic force had possessed her! Instead, she had become the latest victim of mystery illness. (END Studio Intro)

Until a year ago ANGELICA lived a normal life; had a regular job; and was in a loving relationship, until a catastrophic and virtually unknown disease took her out of her reality, and she lost 4 months of her life.

Close family friend captured these moments during Angelica’s lock down in 2014

Leading up to her illness, Angelica’s symptoms were unremarkable: she’d had a dose of tonsillitis and been on 2 courses of antibiotics. It was Angelica’s girlfriend, Tracey who raised the red flag, last year.

It turned out that Angelica was in the grips of an uncommon brain disease. This condition presents with such radical symptoms that it is no surprise to see it confused with psychiatric mental disorder.

First recognized by the medical world as recently as 2007, it is, in fact, a rare form of encephalitis known as Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis. Dr. ANDRE MOCHAN, explained that the condition is, in fact, autoimmune.
This was only the beginning of Angelica’s terror.

But the neurologist was unable to shed much light, and no one could have predicted what happened next.

From one facility to the next her behavior got progressively bizarre. The next stop was Rand Clinic.

At Poortview Hospital in Roodepoort, it was the words of Psychiatrist, DR. ALMA KALABA, that would take the journey in a whole new direction

Locally, the disease is so rare that Dr Mochan has only heard of 3 or 4 patients.

Angelica’s story may be rare, but across the Atlantic, in New York, a young newspaper reporter went through a very similar ordeal, her brain was also on fire.

SUSANNAH CAHALAN was the 217th person reported in the world with this rare condition. She was able to piece together her lost memories of her month of madness in her book BRAIN ON FIRE, which shot to the top of the New York Times Bestseller list.

Susannah’s early symptoms also gave little cause for concern.

It was the bright lights of Times Square that first caused Susannah to realize something serious was at play.

Susannah’s behavior became increasingly unnatural, and after visiting a dozen doctors, New York neurologist, Dr. Najjar, finally uncovered the underlying cause of her behavior.

Both Angelica and Susannah received a host of outrageous diagnoses from mad cow disease, to alcohol withdrawal, and poisoning.

DEREK LINK (on couch) the roller coaster of medical treatments would cost Susannah and her family more than a $1m, but it was a simple pencil drawing that showed clearly why her brain was on fire.

A major breakthrough occurred when Dr. Najjar simply asked her to draw the face of a clock.

DEREK Q&A with Dr Najjar how does the drawing of a clock help provide another clue to this illness?

When the disease was named by Dr JOSEP DALMAU in 2007 there were only 12 reported cases in the U.S. Later diagnoses increased exponentially.
This begs the question: how can diagnosis and treatment be improved on. Dr. Najjar believes the most important thing is to have a high index of suspicion, and not just assume that it is a “regular” psychosis.

At WILGEHEUWAL HOSPITAL Jaqui and Tracey’s nightmare escalated.

Ironically it was the ONE thing that Angelica insisted her family never inflict on her, a SPINAL TAP, which saved her life. Her spinal fluid samples were couriered to a specialist lab in Germany. Meanwhile, a brain biopsy had been scheduled.

Before they could treat Angelica’s psychosis they had to treat her medical condition, the encephalitis. Plasma exchange flushed out the abnormal antibodies.

During this grim period when Angelica was in treatment, her family did everything they could to keep her with them. Even if only in the most basic way, Angelica’s Guardian, JEAN DE LA HARPE, tried to remind her of her identity.

DEREK REVERSAL you were taking notes as well

At a more developed stage Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis can effect more than brain functions. Ranging from abnormal blood pressure fluctuations to heart rhythm, and even breathing, at which point, patients require ICU management.

But even when it’s been diagnosed it seems the treatment is still a very complicated affair, and could recur.

After a 4 month odyssey where she was strapped down, locked up in isolation, and believed she was the Head of Google, Angelica returned to her world with the capacity of a 12 year old. Without memory of the nightmare, that person in lock down will always be a stranger.

Angelica and Susannah’s stories may be harrowing, but what if they are the lucky ones? What if there are hundreds or thousands of patients wallowing in psychiatric hospitals for the rest of their lives all because they didn't get the right treatment

PROMO SCRIPTS/SOUND-UPS (3 x 10”)

#1 JACKIE GEFFIN (Mother) I/V Bite:
Sound-Up .…A MOTHER GRAPPLES WITH HER DAUGHTER’S SUDDEN PYSCHOSIS

#2 SUSANNAH CAHALAN (US Author) I/V Bite and hospital footage
Sound-Up …..A DISEASE OF THE MIND, SETS THE BRAIN ABLAZE

#3 ANGELICA ARAUJO (Subject) I/V Bite: It went from gradual memory loss to extreme ...
Sound-Up …….HOW DOES ONE LOSE THEIR SANITY OVERNIGHT?
